---
title: "code, data & environment versioning"
---

## what should a rerun preserve?

- keep the code revision, input snapshot, reference files, configuration, split rules, and environment
- record seeds and hardware; exact numerical agreement can still depend on libraries, parallelism, and algorithms
- define what counts as agreement: identical files, matching predictions within a tolerance, or comparable evaluation results

## environment vocabulary

- a container image is a packaged filesystem and configuration used to create containers; a container is an instance of that image, useful for running a tool with its dependencies [docker image basics](https://docs.docker.com/get-started/docker-concepts/the-basics/what-is-an-image/)
- an image tag is a human-readable label that can be reassigned; a digest is a content-based identifier used to select an exact image
- a container runtime is software that creates and runs containers; apptainer is a runtime designed for scientific and hpc workflows
- hpc means high-performance computing, often a shared cluster; a scheduler allocates resources among submitted jobs
- an executor is the nextflow component that launches tasks through a chosen execution system; a profile is a named group of settings used to switch environments

## nextflow, docker & slurm

::: {.table-responsive tabindex="0"}

| tool | what it is | when to use it |
|---|---|---|
| nextflow | a workflow engine for connected processes | coordinate sequencing quality checks, alignment, and quantification steps |
| docker | a platform for building and running containers | package a tool and its dependencies for a repeatable environment |
| slurm | a cluster workload manager and job scheduler | queue analyses and request cpu, memory, and time allocations |

:::

- retain the nextflow version and reports, docker image digest and build inputs, and slurm job ids and logs with the run [slurm overview](https://slurm.schedmd.com/overview.html)
- a reference genome is an assembly used as a coordinate and sequence reference, for example during alignment
- an annotation describes features such as genes and exons; use a version compatible with the reference when quantifying expression
- a sample sheet maps sample identifiers to files and metadata; use it to keep inputs correctly associated with samples
- version these files and tool settings together
- changing a reference file can change results even when the workflow code is unchanged

## a small nextflow configuration

- this `nextflow.config` fragment belongs beside an existing `main.nf` workflow
- `local_docker` requires docker on the local machine; the `hpc` profile requires access to a slurm cluster and a suitable software environment

```groovy
profiles {
    local_docker {
        process.executor = 'local'
        docker.enabled = true
        // set process.container in your workflow to the required image
    }
    hpc {
        process.executor = 'slurm'
        process.cpus = 2
        process.memory = '4 GB'
        process.time = '1h'
    }
}
```

- nextflow submits tasks through its selected executor; slurm allocates the requested resources [executor guide](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/executor), [slurm guide](https://slurm.schedmd.com/quickstart.html)
- this example does not enable containers for `hpc`; configure the runtime supported by your cluster, such as apptainer, and provide software environments for every process [container options](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/container)

```bash
# with an existing workflow and configured process containers
nextflow run main.nf -profile local_docker -with-report report.html -with-trace trace.tsv
# resume eligible tasks from that run
nextflow run main.nf -profile local_docker -resume
```

- a task cache stores metadata used to recognise reusable work; resume reuses eligible completed tasks so an interrupted workflow need not start over
- resume needs both the cache and corresponding work outputs; it is a recovery feature rather than an independent rerun from scratch [cache and resume](https://docs.seqera.io/nextflow/cache-and-resume)
- pin container images by digest for an exact image version; tags can change, and image pinning alone does not fix input data or hardware differences [docker image pinning](https://docs.docker.com/build/building/best-practices/)

## check reproducibility

- rerun a small fixed dataset in a fresh output location
- compare outputs or metrics using a tolerance appropriate to the task
- investigate differences in code, inputs, configuration, references, and environment before attributing them to randomness
- a run manifest is a structured record of inputs, settings, environment, and output locations; use it to link a result to the [dataset version](../data-pipelines/versioning.qmd)
